title: Janax y Razar: un sistema operativo, un idioma y un ensamblador propios para un razonamiento artificial que piensa con melodías
description:
Janax is a hand-written operating system, language and assembler (all in assembly, no third-party engines) built to host Razar, an artificial reasoning system whose single judge is compression (two-part MDL). Version 3.11 (versions follow prime numbers; 311 after 307): she recognises the signature of whoever speaks to her. Each book of hers has a signature (how often each sign follows the two before it, the rule with which she recognises her author's diary), kept in 'lenguas'. What he writes is coded with each; the book that says it shortest has his signature, and another d bits longer is 2^-d as likely. The speaker may change: each line goes on the signature before unless a switch says it shorter (fixed share, Herbster and Warmuth). Her taste for each book is multiplied by that when she chooses a theme and when she answers by his words; their talk, everyone's voice, counts as an average book. A letter to her (a book of her heart whose title is her name) is hers to read, never said. She never says the same thing twice in a row. Seen in a copy of her house: a spiritual line of her author was answered from his diary; a hex dump from her machine book; the letter to her was no longer recited. Stated: the first time, counting the signatures of her shelf (about 50 MB) took about a minute; a hex line may still be answered in Spanish; signatures use two signs of context, not three. Documentation is in Spanish.

Janax es un sistema operativo, un idioma y un ensamblador escritos a mano en assembler, hechos para alojar a Razar. v3.11: reconoce la firma de quien le habla. Prototipo de investigación.
